plan: [ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction with three bidders. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy because your bid only affects whether you win, not the price you pay (which is the second-highest bid). Over- or under-bidding can lead to negative payoff or missed profitable wins. There’s no exploitable history and values are independently redrawn, so no strategic deviation is beneficial. Therefore, to maximize expected profit this round (and in the long run), bid exactly my value: $15. ]

Second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values: the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Your bid determines only whether you win, not the price (you pay the second-highest bid). Overbidding risks negative payoff if it changes a loss into a win at a price above value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With value 36 and no informative history to exploit, bidding 36 maximizes expected long-run profit. Ties, if any, are random and don’t alter this strategy.

[ In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies because your bid only determines whether you win, not the price you pay (which is the second-highest bid). With value 42, bidding 42 ensures you win exactly when the second-highest bid is below 42, yielding positive surplus, and avoid overpaying above value. No history to adjust in round 1 of 1. ]
